# Calendar

Calendar — the month grid DatePicker and DateTimePicker open (Figma `_Calendar`), public for a caller who wants the grid on its own rather than behind a field's popup. It is the same component the pickers use. - **Grid:** always six weeks, 42 cells, so the panel never changes height. Days of the months either side are drawn and can't be picked. - **Days:** each is a button named with its full date. `aria-pressed` marks the picked day, or both ends of a range; `data-in-range` marks the days between; `aria-current="date"` marks today. - **Bounds:** days before `minDate` or after `maxDate` are disabled. - **Size:** a pixel width, 28, 36 or 44, drawn from the `--calendar-day-*` tokens.

**Import:** `import { Calendar } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Calendar/Calendar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Calendar/Calendar.stories.jsx` — Size28, Size36, Size44, PickADay, TurnMonths, Default, Selected, Range, Disabled, HoveredState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

## Usage

Use a calendar directly only when a date grid needs to be visible on the page without a field or a popup around it: a scheduling view, an embedded picker. For a single date field, use Date picker; for a date and time together, use Date time picker. Both already use this same grid.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say which dates can be chosen in text near the calendar: "Pick a day between October 12 and 25." | Leave people to find the limit by trying disabled days. |
| Name the choice by its role: "Session date". | "Calendar" or "Pick a date". |
| Write dates in full where text names them: "October 21, 2026". | All-numeric dates that read differently by locale: "10/11/12". |

## Best practices

### Name the month in full, with the year. {#name-the-month-in-full-with-the-year}

The header says which month the grid shows, such as "October 2026". The calendar writes it this way itself; numbers alone make people count.

### Dim unavailable days, do not hide them. {#dim-unavailable-days-do-not-hide-them}

A dimmed day tells people why a slot is missing; a day that looks pickable but is not wastes a tap. Set `minDate` and `maxDate` to the span that can be chosen.

Do: Days outside the span that can be chosen are dimmed and disabled.
Don't: Every day looks pickable, and the limit is found only after an error.

### Show the selected date as one filled day. {#show-the-selected-date-as-one-filled-day}

In single mode one day carries the selected fill. A second fill reads as a range.

Do: One picked day carries the fill.
Don't: Two filled ends for a single answer read as a range.

### Say which dates can be chosen. {#say-which-dates-can-be-chosen}

Put the limit in text near the calendar, so people do not find it by trying disabled days.

Do: A line above the grid states the span.
Don't: No text: the limit shows only as dimmed days.

### Let the caller own the month on show. {#let-the-caller-own-the-month-on-show}

`Calendar` holds no state of its own. The caller owns `viewDate` and updates it when `onViewDateChange` fires, the same pattern Date picker uses internally.

```jsx
const [viewDate, setViewDate] = useState(new Date());

<Calendar
    viewDate={viewDate}
    onViewDateChange={setViewDate}
    selected={selectedDate}
    onPick={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

### Keep the grid at six weeks. {#keep-the-grid-at-six-weeks}

Six weeks render every month, including the days of neighboring months that fill the remaining cells. This keeps the panel's height constant as someone pages through months, at the cost of occasionally showing a mostly empty week.

## Accessibility

- **Each day is a real, named button.** The accessible name is the day's full date, not just a number, so a screen reader announces an unambiguous date on every cell.
- **State is marked, not just styled.** `aria-pressed` marks the picked day or a range's ends, `aria-current="date"` marks today, and `data-in-range` marks the days between. None of this relies on color alone.
- **Out-of-range and out-of-month days are truly disabled**, not just dimmed: they take no focus and fire no `onPick`.
- **The month buttons are named** "Previous month" and "Next month".

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `viewDate` | instanceOf (required) | — | Any day in the month on show. |
| `onViewDateChange` | func (required) | — | `(firstOfMonth)` when Previous month or Next month is pressed. |
| `selected` | string or instanceOf | — | The picked day, as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or a Date. |
| `rangeStart` | string or instanceOf | — | A range's first day; with `rangeEnd`, the days between are marked. |
| `rangeEnd` | string or instanceOf | — | — |
| `minDate` | string or instanceOf | — | The earliest day that can be picked, as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or a Date. Earlier days are disabled. |
| `maxDate` | string or instanceOf | — | The latest day that can be picked, as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or a Date. Later days are disabled. |
| `size` | enum | — | Day width in pixels: 28, 36 or 44. |
| `onPick` | func (required) | — | `(date)` when an enabled day is pressed. |
| `className` | string | — | — |
